message.content:
The freezing (melting) point of water decreases only slightly as the pressure is lowered.  
At the triple‑point pressure of 6.112 kPa the freezing point is about +0.01 °C.  
At 10 kPa the freezing point is only a little lower – roughly **–0.2 °C** (≈ –0.2 °C ± 0.1 °C depending on the exact thermodynamic data used).

So, at 10 kPa the water will freeze at just below 0 °C, around –0.2 °C.
